The stochastic model is integrated into the AeroDyn software as an alternative to the classical BEM and dynamic stall models.
The stochastic model parameters are derived from dynamic measurements of lift and drag forces performed for the FX79-W-151A airfoil in a wind tunnel with 4.6% turbulence intensity.

The stochastic model represents the lift and drag coefficients as a first-order stochastic differential equation (Langevin equation) with drift and diffusion functions parameterized as functions of the mean angle of attack.
The stochastic model includes an extension to account for oscillation effects with amplitude modulation (breathing) contained in the lift and drag time series.
The induction factors are estimated using an iterative process described in a flow chart, where the axial and tangential induction factors are calculated until they converge to their final values.
The full field turbulence simulated wind data is generated by the TurbSim program, which provides the three wind velocity components changing in time and space across the rotor area.
The simulations are performed for a 3-bladed wind turbine with a rotor radius of 13.76 m, divided into 10 equal segments along the radius.
The increment probability density functions (PDFs) of the stochastic model results show slight to pronounced heavier tails compared to the normal distribution, indicating intermittent behavior.
The kurtosis and standard deviations of the increment signals for the stochastic model show slight to pronounced higher positive kurtosis, meaning the PDFs have heavier tails.

The simulations consider various degrees of freedom in the wind turbine model, including first and second flapwise and edgewise blade modes, drivetrain rotational flexibility, generator, yaw, and tower bending modes.
The interpolated hub-height turbulence intensity of the wind input data used in the simulations is 15%.
The stochastic model generates additional dynamic response in terms of local force fluctuations compared to the classical BEM and dynamic stall models.
The classical BEM model captures the mean force dynamics, while the dynamic stall model captures small fluctuations around the mean.
The stochastic model is integrated into AeroDyn, which is called by the FAST dynamic analysis program to perform the aerodynamic calculations.
The airfoil data file in AeroDyn is replaced with the measured aerodynamic characteristics of the FX79-W-151A airfoil for comparison purposes.
